bsb.13:5: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend you are ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare it in my sight so I may watch her and eat it from her hand.’”
bsb.13:6: So Amnon lay down and feigned illness. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in my sight, so that I may eat from her hand.”
bsb.13:7: Then David sent word to Tamar at the palace: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare a meal for him.”
bsb.13:8: So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked them.
bsb.13:9: Then she brought the pan and set it down before him, but he refused to eat. “Send everyone away!” said Amnon. And everyone went out.
bsb.13:10: Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the bedroom, so that I may eat it from your hand.” Tamar took the cakes she had made and went to her brother Amnon’s bedroom.
bsb.13:11: And when she had brought them to him to eat, he took hold of her and said, “Come lie with me, my sister!”
bsb.13:12: “No, my brother!” she cried. “Do not humiliate me, for such a thing should never be done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing!
bsb.13:13: Where could I ever take my shame? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel! Please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.”
bsb.13:14: But Amnon refused to listen to her, and being stronger, he violated her and lay with her.
bsb.13:15: Then Amnon hated Tamar with such intensity that his hatred was greater than the love he previously had. “Get up!” he said to her. “Be gone!”
bsb.13:16: “No,” she replied, “sending me away is worse than this great wrong you have already done to me!” But he refused to listen to her.
bsb.13:17: Instead, he called to his attendant and said, “Throw this woman out and bolt the door behind her!”
bsb.13:18: So Amnon’s attendant threw her out and bolted the door behind her. Now Tamar was wearing a robe of many colors, because this is what the king’s virgin daughters wore.
bsb.13:19: And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her robe. And putting her hand on her head, she went away crying bitterly.
bsb.13:20: Her brother Absalom said to her, “Has your brother Amnon been with you? Be quiet for now, my sister. He is your brother. Do not take this thing to heart.” So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.
bsb.13:21: When King David heard all this, he was furious.
bsb.13:22: And Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad, because he hated Amnon for disgracing his sister Tamar.
bsb.13:23: Two years later, when Absalom’s sheepshearers were at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, he invited all the sons of the king.
bsb.13:24: And he went to the king and said, “Your servant has just hired shearers. Will the king and his servants please come with me?”
bsb.13:25: “No, my son,” the king replied, “we should not all go, or we would be a burden to you.” Although Absalom urged him, he was not willing to go, but gave him his blessing.
bsb.13:26: “If not,” said Absalom, “please let my brother Amnon go with us.” “Why should he go with you?” the king asked.
bsb.13:27: But Absalom urged him, so the king sent Amnon and the rest of his sons.
bsb.13:28: Now Absalom had ordered his young men, “Watch Amnon until his heart is merry with wine, and when I order you to strike Amnon down, you are to kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!”
bsb.13:29: So Absalom’s young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had ordered. Then all the other sons of the king got up, and each one fled on his mule.
bsb.13:30: While they were on the way, a report reached David: “Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king; not one of them is left!”
bsb.13:31: Then the king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground; and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.
bsb.13:32: But Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah, spoke up: “My lord must not think they have killed all the sons of the king, for only Amnon is dead. In fact, Absalom has planned this since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
bsb.13:33: So now, my lord the king, do not take to heart the report that all the sons of the king are dead. Only Amnon is dead.”
bsb.13:34: Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. When the young man standing watch looked up, he saw many people coming down the road west of him, along the side of the hill. And the watchman went and reported to the king, “I see men coming from the direction of Horonaim, along the side of the hill.”
bsb.13:35: So Jonadab said to the king, “Look, the sons of the king have arrived! It is just as your servant said.”
bsb.13:36: And as he finished speaking, the sons of the king came in, wailing loudly. Then the king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.
bsb.13:37: Now Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. But David mourned for his son every day.
bsb.13:38: After Absalom had fled and gone to Geshur, he stayed there three years.
bsb.13:39: And King David longed to go to Absalom, for he had been consoled over Amnon’s death.
bsb.14:1: Now Joab son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart longed for Absalom.
bsb.14:2: So Joab sent to Tekoa to bring a wise woman from there. He told her, “Please pretend to be a mourner; put on clothes for mourning and do not anoint yourself with oil. Act like a woman who has mourned for the dead a long time.
bsb.14:3: Then go to the king and speak these words to him.” And Joab put the words in her mouth.
bsb.14:4: When the woman from Tekoa went to the king, she fell facedown in homage and said, “Help me, O king!”
bsb.14:5: “What troubles you?” the king asked her. “Indeed,” she said, “I am a widow, for my husband is dead.
bsb.14:6: And your maidservant had two sons who were fighting in the field with no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him.
bsb.14:7: Now the whole clan has risen up against your maidservant and said, ‘Hand over the one who struck down his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of the brother whom he killed. Then we will cut off the heir as well!’ So they would extinguish my one remaining ember by not preserving my husband’s name or posterity on the earth.”
bsb.14:8: “Go home,” the king said to the woman, “and I will give orders on your behalf.”
bsb.14:9: But the woman of Tekoa said to the king, “My lord the king, may any blame be on me and on my father’s house, and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”
bsb.14:10: “If anyone speaks to you,” said the king, “bring him to me, and he will not trouble you again!”
bsb.14:11: “Please,” she replied, “may the king invoke the LORD your God to prevent the avenger of blood from increasing the devastation, so that my son may not be destroyed!” “As surely as the LORD lives,” he vowed, “not a hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”
bsb.14:12: Then the woman said, “Please, may your servant speak a word to my lord the king?” “Speak,” he replied.
bsb.14:13: The woman asked, “Why have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, since he has not brought back his own banished son?
bsb.14:14: For surely we will die and be like water poured out on the ground, which cannot be recovered. Yet God does not take away a life; but He devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him.
bsb.14:15: Now therefore, I have come to present this matter to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king. Perhaps he will grant the request of his maidservant.
bsb.14:16: For the king will hear and deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man who would cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’
bsb.14:17: And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king bring me rest, for my lord the king is able to discern good and evil, just like the angel of God. May the LORD your God be with you.’”
bsb.14:18: Then the king said to the woman, “I am going to ask you something; do not conceal it from me!” “Let my lord the king speak,” she replied.
bsb.14:19: So the king asked, “Is the hand of Joab behind all this?” The woman answered, “As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything that my lord the king says. Yes, your servant Joab is the one who gave me orders; he told your maidservant exactly what to say.
bsb.14:20: Joab your servant has done this to bring about this change of affairs, but my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God, to know everything that happens in the land.”
bsb.14:21: Then the king said to Joab, “I hereby grant this request. Go, bring back the young man Absalom.”
bsb.14:22: Joab fell facedown in homage and blessed the king. “Today,” said Joab, “your servant knows that he has found favor with you, my lord the king, because the king has granted his request.”
bsb.14:23: So Joab got up, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
bsb.14:24: But the king added, “He may return to his house, but he must not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his own house, but he did not see the king.
bsb.14:25: Now there was not a man in all Israel as handsome and highly praised as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the top of his head, he did not have a single flaw.
bsb.14:26: And when he cut the hair of his head—he shaved it every year because his hair got so heavy—he would weigh it out to be two hundred shekels, according to the royal standard.
bsb.14:27: Three sons were born to Absalom, and a daughter named Tamar, who was a beautiful woman.
bsb.14:28: Now Absalom lived in Jerusalem two years without seeing the face of the king.
bsb.14:29: Then he sent for Joab to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So Absalom sent a second time, but Joab still would not come.
bsb.14:30: Then Absalom said to his servants, “Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire!” And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
bsb.14:31: Then Joab came to Absalom’s house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
bsb.14:32: “Look,” said Absalom, “I sent for you and said, ‘Come here. I want to send you to the king to ask: Why have I come back from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there.’ So now, let me see the king’s face, and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”
bsb.14:33: So Joab went and told the king, and David summoned Absalom, who came to him and bowed facedown before him. Then the king kissed Absalom.
bsb.15:1: Some time later, Absalom provided for himself a chariot with horses and fifty men to run ahead of him.
bsb.15:2: He would get up early and stand beside the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone had a grievance to bring before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out and ask, “What city are you from?” And if he replied, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,”
bsb.15:3: Absalom would say, “Look, your claims are good and right, but the king has no deputy to hear you.”
bsb.15:4: And he would add, “If only someone would appoint me judge in the land, then everyone with a grievance or dispute could come to me, and I would give him justice.”
bsb.15:5: Also, when anyone approached to bow down to him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.
bsb.15:6: Absalom did this to all the Israelites who came to the king for justice. In this way he stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
bsb.15:7: After four years had passed, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go to Hebron to fulfill a vow I have made to the LORD.
bsb.15:8: For your servant made a vow while dwelling in Geshur of Aram, saying: ‘If indeed the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.’”
bsb.15:9: “Go in peace,” said the king. So Absalom got up and went to Hebron.
bsb.15:10: Then Absalom sent spies throughout the tribes of Israel with this message: “When you hear the sound of the horn, you are to say, ‘Absalom reigns in Hebron!’”
bsb.15:11: Two hundred men from Jerusalem accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and they went along innocently, for they knew nothing about the matter.
bsb.15:12: While Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from his hometown of Giloh. So the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept increasing.
bsb.15:13: Then a messenger came to David and reported, “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”
bsb.15:14: And David said to all the servants with him in Jerusalem, “Arise and let us flee, or we will not escape from Absalom! We must leave quickly, or he will soon overtake us, heap disaster on us, and put the city to the sword.”
bsb.15:15: The king’s servants replied, “Whatever our lord the king decides, we are your servants.”
bsb.15:16: Then the king set out, and his entire household followed him. But he left behind ten concubines to take care of the palace.
bsb.15:17: So the king set out with all the people following him. He stopped at the last house,
bsb.15:18: and all his servants marched past him—all the Cherethites and Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath.
bsb.15:19: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you also go with us? Go back and stay with the new king, since you are both a foreigner and an exile from your homeland.
bsb.15:20: In fact, you arrived only yesterday; should I make you wander around with us today while I do not know where I am going? Go back and take your brothers with you. May the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness.”
bsb.15:21: But Ittai answered the king, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be!”
bsb.15:22: “March on then,” said David to Ittai. So Ittai the Gittite marched past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
bsb.15:23: Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly as all the people passed by. And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley, all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.
bsb.15:24: Zadok was also there, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until the people had passed out of the city.
bsb.15:25: Then the king said to Zadok, “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.
bsb.15:26: But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”
bsb.15:27: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace—you with your son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan.
bsb.15:28: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”
bsb.15:29: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there.
bsb.15:30: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up. His head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.
bsb.15:31: Now someone told David: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David pleaded, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”
bsb.15:32: When David came to the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.
bsb.15:33: David said to him, “If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.
bsb.15:34: But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom: ‘I will be your servant, my king; in the past I was your father’s servant, but now I will be your servant.’
bsb.15:35: Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Report to them everything you hear from the king’s palace.
bsb.15:36: Indeed, their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with everything you hear.”
bsb.15:37: So David’s friend Hushai arrived in Jerusalem just as Absalom was entering the city.
bsb.16:1: When David had gone a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
bsb.16:2: “Why do you have these?” asked the king. Ziba replied, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”
bsb.16:3: “Where is your master’s grandson?” asked the king. And Ziba answered, “Indeed, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he has said, ‘Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.’”
bsb.16:4: So the king said to Ziba, “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!” “I humbly bow before you,” said Ziba. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king!”
bsb.16:5: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the family of the house of Saul was just coming out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he approached, he kept yelling out curses.
bsb.16:6: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of the king, though the troops and all the mighty men were on David’s right and left.
bsb.16:7: And as he yelled curses, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you worthless man of bloodshed!
bsb.16:8: The LORD has paid you back for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed!”
bsb.16:9: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head!”
bsb.16:10: But the king replied, “What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses me because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’”
bsb.16:11: Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my own son, my own flesh and blood, seeks my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse me, for the LORD has told him so.
bsb.16:12: Perhaps the LORD will see my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today.”
bsb.16:13: So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him. As Shimei went, he yelled curses, threw stones, and flung dust at David.
bsb.16:14: Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived, exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.
bsb.16:15: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
bsb.16:16: And David’s friend Hushai the Archite went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
bsb.16:17: “Is this the loyalty you show your friend?” Absalom replied. “Why did you not go with your friend?”
bsb.16:18: “Not at all,” Hushai answered. “For the one chosen by the LORD, by the people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and with him I will remain.
bsb.16:19: Furthermore, whom should I serve if not the son? As I served in your father’s presence, so also I will serve in yours.”
bsb.16:20: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give me counsel. What should we do?”
bsb.16:21: Ahithophel replied, “Sleep with your father’s concubines, whom he has left to keep the palace. When all Israel hears that you have become a stench to your father, then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”
bsb.16:22: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
bsb.16:23: Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel was like the consultation of the word of God. Such was the regard that both David and Absalom had for Ahithophel’s advice.
bsb.17:1: Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.
bsb.17:2: I will attack him while he is weak and weary; I will throw him into a panic, and all the people with him will flee; I will strike down only the king
bsb.17:3: and bring all the people back to you as a bride returning to her husband. You seek the life of only one man; then all the people will be at peace.”
bsb.17:4: This proposal seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
bsb.17:5: Then Absalom said, “Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say.”
bsb.17:6: So Hushai came to Absalom, who told him, “Ahithophel has spoken this proposal. Should we carry it out? If not, what do you say?”
bsb.17:7: Hushai replied, “This time the advice of Ahithophel is not sound.”
bsb.17:8: He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.
bsb.17:9: Surely by now he is hiding in a cave or some other location. If some of your troops fall first, whoever hears of it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’
bsb.17:10: Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear, because all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man who has valiant men with him.
bsb.17:11: Instead, I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba—a multitude like the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, and that you yourself lead them into battle.
bsb.17:12: Then we will attack David wherever we find him, and we will descend on him like dew on the ground. And of all the men with him, not even one will remain.
bsb.17:13: If he retreats to a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found.”
bsb.17:14: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.
bsb.17:15: So Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “This is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I have advised.
bsb.17:16: Now send quickly and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over. Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’”
bsb.17:17: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, where a servant girl would come and pass along information to them. They in turn would go and inform King David, for they dared not be seen entering the city.
bsb.17:18: But a young man did see them and told Absalom. So the two left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.
bsb.17:19: Then the man’s wife took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, scattering grain over it so nobody would know a thing.
bsb.17:20: When Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” “They have crossed over the brook,” she replied. The men searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.
bsb.17:21: After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David, saying, “Get up and cross over the river at once, for Ahithophel has given this advice against you.”
bsb.17:22: So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan.
bsb.17:23: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his affairs in order and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.
bsb.17:24: Then David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
bsb.17:25: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra, the Ishmaelite who had married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.
bsb.17:26: So the Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
bsb.17:27: When David came to Mahanaim, he was met by Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim.
bsb.17:28: They brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, as well as wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils,
bsb.17:29: honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become hungry, exhausted, and thirsty in the wilderness.”
bsb.18:1: Then David reviewed his troops and appointed over them commanders of hundreds and of thousands.
bsb.18:2: He sent out the troops, a third under Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the troops, “I will surely march out with you as well.”
bsb.18:3: But the people pleaded, “You must not go out! For if we have to flee, they will pay no attention to us. Even if half of us die, they will not care; but you are worth ten thousand of us. It is better for now if you support us from the city.”
bsb.18:4: “I will do whatever seems best to you,” the king replied. So he stood beside the gate, while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
bsb.18:5: Now the king had commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake.” And all the people heard the king’s orders to each of the commanders regarding Absalom.
bsb.18:6: So David’s army marched into the field to engage Israel in the battle, which took place in the forest of Ephraim.
bsb.18:7: There the people of Israel were defeated by David’s servants, and the slaughter was great that day—twenty thousand men.
bsb.18:8: The battle spread over the whole countryside, and that day the forest devoured more people than the sword.
bsb.18:9: Now Absalom was riding on his mule when he met the servants of David, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree. The mule under him kept going, so that he was suspended in midair.
bsb.18:10: When one of the men saw this, he told Joab, “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree!”
bsb.18:11: “You just saw him!” Joab exclaimed. “Why did you not strike him to the ground right there? I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt!”
bsb.18:12: The man replied, “Even if a thousand shekels of silver were weighed out into my hands, I would not raise my hand against the son of the king. For we heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.’
bsb.18:13: If I had jeopardized my own life—and nothing is hidden from the king—you would have abandoned me.”
bsb.18:14: But Joab declared, “I am not going to wait like this with you!” And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.
bsb.18:15: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
bsb.18:16: Then Joab blew the ram’s horn, and the troops broke off their pursuit of Israel because Joab had restrained them.
bsb.18:17: They took Absalom, cast him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge mound of stones over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled, each to his home.
bsb.18:18: During his lifetime, Absalom had set up for himself a pillar in the King’s Valley, for he had said, “I have no son to preserve the memory of my name.” So he gave the pillar his name, and to this day it is called Absalom’s Monument.
bsb.18:19: Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Please let me run and tell the king the good news that the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.”
bsb.18:20: But Joab replied, “You are not the man to take good news today. You may do it another day, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead.”
bsb.18:21: So Joab said to a Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” The Cushite bowed to Joab and took off running.
bsb.18:22: Ahimaaz son of Zadok, however, persisted and said to Joab, “Regardless of whatever may happen, please let me also run behind the Cushite!” “My son,” Joab replied, “why do you want to run, since you will not receive a reward?”
bsb.18:23: “No matter what, I want to run!” he replied. “Then run!” Joab told him. So Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
bsb.18:24: Now David was sitting between the two gates when the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall, looked out, and saw a man running alone.
bsb.18:25: So he called out and told the king. “If he is alone,” the king replied, “he bears good news.” As the first runner drew near,
bsb.18:26: the watchman saw another man running, and he called out to the gatekeeper, “Look! Another man is running alone!” “This one also brings good news,” said the king.
bsb.18:27: The watchman said, “The first man appears to me to be running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.” “This is a good man,” said the king. “He comes with good news.”
bsb.18:28: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All is well!” And he bowed facedown before the king. He continued, “Blessed be the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who raised their hands against my lord the king.”
bsb.18:29: The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And Ahimaaz replied, “When Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was.”
bsb.18:30: “Move aside,” said the king, “and stand here.” So he stepped aside.
bsb.18:31: Just then the Cushite came and said, “May my lord the king hear the good news: Today the LORD has avenged you of all who rose up against you!”
bsb.18:32: The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And the Cushite replied, “May what has become of the young man happen to the enemies of my lord the king and to all who rise up against you to harm you.”
bsb.18:33: The king was shaken and went up to the gate chamber and wept. And as he walked, he cried out, “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!”
bsb.19:1: Then it was reported to Joab, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”
bsb.19:2: And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people, because on that day they were told, “The king is grieving over his son.”
bsb.19:3: So they returned to the city quietly that day, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle.
bsb.19:4: But the king covered his face and cried out at the top of his voice, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”
bsb.19:5: Then Joab went into the house and said to the king, “Today you have disgraced all your servants who have saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, of your wives, and of your concubines.
bsb.19:6: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you! For you have made it clear today that the commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, it would have pleased you!
bsb.19:7: Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants, for I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight. This will be worse for you than all the adversity that has befallen you from your youth until now!”
bsb.19:8: So the king got up and sat in the gate, and all the people were told: “Behold, the king is sitting in the gate.” So they all came before the king. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled, each man to his home.
bsb.19:9: And all the people throughout the tribes of Israel were arguing, “The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, but now he has fled the land because of Absalom.
bsb.19:10: But Absalom, the man we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about restoring the king?”
bsb.19:11: Then King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: “Say to the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to restore the king to his palace, since the talk of all Israel has reached the king at his quarters?
bsb.19:12: You are my brothers, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to restore the king?’
bsb.19:13: And say to Amasa, ‘Aren’t you my flesh and blood? May God punish me, and ever so severely, if from this time you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab!’”
bsb.19:14: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man, and they sent word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.”
bsb.19:15: So the king returned, and when he arrived at the Jordan, the men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the Jordan.
bsb.19:16: Then Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David,
bsb.19:17: along with a thousand men of Benjamin, as well as Ziba the steward of the house of Saul and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan before the king
bsb.19:18: and crossed at the ford to carry over the king’s household and to do what was good in his sight. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell down before the king
bsb.19:19: and said, “My lord, do not hold me guilty, and do not remember your servant’s wrongdoing on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king not take it to heart.
bsb.19:20: For your servant knows that I have sinned, so here I am today as the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”
bsb.19:21: But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”
bsb.19:22: And David replied, “Sons of Zeruiah, what have I to do with you, that you should be my adversaries today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel?”
bsb.19:23: So the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” And the king swore an oath to him.
bsb.19:24: Then Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, went down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king had left until the day he returned safely.
bsb.19:25: And he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, who asked him, “Mephibosheth, why did you not go with me?”
bsb.19:26: “My lord the king,” he replied, “because I am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled so that I may ride on it and go with the king.’ But my servant Ziba deceived me,
bsb.19:27: and he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. Yet my lord the king is like the angel of God, so do what is good in your eyes.
bsb.19:28: For all the house of my grandfather deserves death from my lord the king, yet you have set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right, then, do I have to keep appealing to the king?”
bsb.19:29: The king replied, “Why say any more? I hereby declare that you and Ziba are to divide the land.”
bsb.19:30: And Mephibosheth said to the king, “Instead, since my lord the king has safely come to his own house, let Ziba take it all!”
bsb.19:31: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and send him on his way from there.
bsb.19:32: Barzillai was quite old, eighty years of age, and since he was a very wealthy man, he had provided for the king while he stayed in Mahanaim.
bsb.19:33: The king said to Barzillai, “Cross over with me, and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem.”
bsb.19:34: But Barzillai replied, “How many years of my life remain, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?
bsb.19:35: I am now eighty years old. Can I discern what is good and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or drinks? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and women? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?
bsb.19:36: Your servant could go with the king only a short distance past the Jordan; why should the king repay me with such a reward?
bsb.19:37: Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight.”
bsb.19:38: The king replied, “Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him what seems good in your sight, and I will do for you whatever you desire of me.”
bsb.19:39: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned home.
bsb.19:40: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king.
bsb.19:41: Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and asked, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you away secretly and bring the king and his household across the Jordan, together with all of David’s men?”
bsb.19:42: And all the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel, “We did this because the king is our relative. Why does this anger you? Have we ever eaten at the king’s expense or received anything for ourselves?”
bsb.19:43: “We have ten shares in the king,” answered the men of Israel, “so we have more claim to David than you. Why then do you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of restoring our king?” But the men of Judah pressed even harder than the men of Israel.
bsb.20:1: Now a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite, happened to be there, and he blew the ram’s horn and shouted: “We have no share in David, no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his tent, O Israel!”
bsb.20:2: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
bsb.20:3: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to care for the palace, and he placed them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but he no longer slept with them. They were confined until the day of their death, living as widows.
bsb.20:4: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”
bsb.20:5: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time allotted him.
bsb.20:6: And David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and elude us.”
bsb.20:7: So Joab’s men, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men, marched out of Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
bsb.20:8: And while they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa joined them. Now Joab was dressed in military attire, with a dagger strapped to his belt. And as he stepped forward, he slipped the dagger from its sheath.
bsb.20:9: “Are you well, my brother?” Joab asked Amasa. And with his right hand Joab grabbed Amasa by the beard to kiss him.
bsb.20:10: Amasa was not on guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab stabbed him in the stomach and spilled out his intestines on the ground. And Joab did not need to strike him again, for Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
bsb.20:11: One of Joab’s young men stood near Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”
bsb.20:12: But Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the road, and when the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged the body off the road into a field and threw a garment over it.
bsb.20:13: As soon as Amasa’s body was removed from the road, all the men went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
bsb.20:14: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel-beth-maacah and through the entire region of the Berites, who gathered together and followed him.
bsb.20:15: And Joab’s troops came and besieged Sheba in Abel-beth-maacah and built a siege ramp against the outer rampart of the city. As all the troops with Joab were battering the wall to topple it,
bsb.20:16: a wise woman called out from the city, “Listen! Listen! Please tell Joab to come here so that I may speak with him.”
bsb.20:17: When he had come near to her, the woman asked, “Are you Joab?” “I am,” he replied. “Listen to the words of your servant,” she said. “I am listening,” he answered.
bsb.20:18: Then the woman said, “Long ago they used to say, ‘Seek counsel at Abel,’ and that is how disputes were settled.
bsb.20:19: I am among the peaceable and faithful in Israel, but you are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the LORD’s inheritance?”
bsb.20:20: “Far be it!” Joab declared. “Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!
bsb.20:21: That is not the case. But a man named Sheba son of Bichri, from the hill country of Ephraim, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Deliver him alone, and I will depart from the city.” “Look,” the woman replied, “his head will be thrown to you over the wall.”
bsb.20:22: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. So he blew the ram’s horn and his men dispersed from the city, each to his own home. And Joab returned to the king in Jerusalem.
bsb.20:23: Now Joab was over the whole army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites;
bsb.20:24: Adoram was in charge of the forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
bsb.20:25: Sheva was the scribe; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
bsb.20:26: and Ira the Jairite was David’s priest.
bsb.21:1: During the reign of David there was a famine for three successive years, and David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said, “It is because of the blood shed by Saul and his family, because he killed the Gibeonites.”
bsb.21:2: At this, David summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites, but a remnant of the Amorites. The Israelites had taken an oath concerning them, but in his zeal for Israel and Judah, Saul had sought to kill them.)
bsb.21:3: So David asked the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? How can I make amends so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?”
bsb.21:4: The Gibeonites said to him, “We need no silver or gold from Saul or his house, nor should you put to death anyone in Israel for us.” “Whatever you ask, I will do for you,” he replied.
bsb.21:5: And they answered the king, “As for the man who consumed us and plotted against us to exterminate us from existing within any border of Israel,
bsb.21:6: let seven of his male descendants be delivered to us so that we may hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD.” “I will give them to you,” said the king.
bsb.21:7: Now the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.
bsb.21:8: But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons whom Rizpah daughter of Aiah had borne to Saul, as well as the five sons whom Merab daughter of Saul had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
bsb.21:9: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the hill before the LORD. So all seven of them fell together; they were put to death in the first days of the harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
bsb.21:10: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. From the beginning of the harvest until the rain from heaven poured down on the bodies, she did not allow the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
bsb.21:11: When David was told what Saul’s concubine Rizpah, daughter of Aiah, had done,
bsb.21:12: he went and took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-shan where the Philistines had hung the bodies after they had struck down Saul at Gilboa.
bsb.21:13: So David had the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan brought from there, along with the bones of those who had been hanged.
bsb.21:14: And they buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in Zela in the land of Benjamin, in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish. After they had done everything the king had commanded, God answered their prayers for the land.
bsb.21:15: Once again the Philistines waged war against Israel, and David and his servants went down and fought against the Philistines; but David became exhausted.
bsb.21:16: Then Ishbi-benob, a descendant of Rapha, whose bronze spear weighed three hundred shekels and who was bearing a new sword, resolved to kill David.
bsb.21:17: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then David’s men swore to him, “You must never again go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished.”
bsb.21:18: Some time later at Gob, there was another battle with the Philistines. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, one of the descendants of Rapha.
bsb.21:19: Once again there was a battle with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
bsb.21:20: And there was still another battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He too was descended from Rapha,
bsb.21:21: and when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of David’s brother Shimei killed him.
bsb.21:22: So these four descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants.
bsb.22:1: And David sang this song to the LORD on the day the LORD had delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
bsb.22:2: He said: “The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer.
bsb.22:3: My God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation. My stronghold, my refuge, and my Savior, You save me from violence.
bsb.22:4: I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; so shall I be saved from my enemies.
bsb.22:5: For the waves of death engulfed me; the torrents of chaos overwhelmed me.
bsb.22:6: The cords of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.
bsb.22:7: In my distress I called upon the LORD; I cried out to my God. And from His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for help reached His ears.
bsb.22:8: Then the earth shook and quaked; the foundations of the heavens trembled; they were shaken because He burned with anger.
bsb.22:9: Smoke rose from His nostrils, and consuming fire came from His mouth; glowing coals blazed forth.
bsb.22:10: He parted the heavens and came down with dark clouds beneath His feet.
bsb.22:11: He mounted a cherub and flew; He soared on the wings of the wind.
bsb.22:12: He made darkness a canopy around Him, a gathering of water and thick clouds.
bsb.22:13: From the brightness of His presence coals of fire blazed forth.
bsb.22:14: The LORD thundered from heaven; the voice of the Most High resounded.
bsb.22:15: He shot His arrows and scattered the foes; He hurled lightning and routed them.
bsb.22:16: The channels of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the world were exposed at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of His nostrils.
bsb.22:17: He reached down from on high and took hold of me; He drew me out of deep waters.
bsb.22:18: He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from foes too mighty for me.
bsb.22:19: They confronted me in my day of calamity, but the LORD was my support.
bsb.22:20: He brought me out into the open; He rescued me because He delighted in me.
bsb.22:21: The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness; He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
bsb.22:22: For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not wickedly departed from my God.
bsb.22:23: For all His ordinances are before me; I have not disregarded His statutes.
bsb.22:24: And I have been blameless before Him and kept myself from iniquity.
bsb.22:25: So the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in His sight.
bsb.22:26: To the faithful You show Yourself faithful, to the blameless You show Yourself blameless;
bsb.22:27: to the pure You show Yourself pure, but to the crooked You show Yourself shrewd.
bsb.22:28: You save an afflicted people, but Your eyes are on the haughty to bring them down.
bsb.22:29: For You, O LORD, are my lamp; the LORD lights up my darkness.
bsb.22:30: For in You I can charge an army; with my God I can scale a wall.
bsb.22:31: As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the LORD is flawless. He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
bsb.22:32: For who is God besides the LORD? And who is the Rock except our God?
bsb.22:33: God is my strong fortress and He makes my way clear.
bsb.22:34: He makes my feet like those of a deer and stations me upon the heights.
bsb.22:35: He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
bsb.22:36: You have given me Your shield of salvation, and Your gentleness exalts me.
bsb.22:37: You broaden the path beneath me so that my ankles do not give way.
bsb.22:38: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them; I did not turn back until they were consumed.
bsb.22:39: I devoured and crushed them so they could not rise; they have fallen under my feet.
bsb.22:40: You have armed me with strength for battle; You have subdued my foes beneath me.
bsb.22:41: You have made my enemies retreat before me; I put an end to those who hated me.
bsb.22:42: They looked, but there was no one to save them— to the LORD, but He did not answer.
bsb.22:43: I ground them as the dust of the earth; I crushed and trampled them like mud in the streets.
bsb.22:44: You have delivered me from the strife of my people; You have preserved me as the head of nations; a people I had not known shall serve me.
bsb.22:45: Foreigners cower before me; when they hear me, they obey me.
bsb.22:46: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling from their strongholds.
bsb.22:47: The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock! And may God, the Rock of my salvation, be exalted—
bsb.22:48: the God who avenges me and brings down nations beneath me,
bsb.22:49: who frees me from my enemies. You exalt me above my foes; You rescue me from violent men.
bsb.22:50: Therefore I will praise You, O LORD, among the nations; I will sing praises to Your name.
bsb.22:51: Great salvation He brings to His king. He shows loving devotion to His anointed, to David and his descendants forever.”
bsb.23:1: These are the last words of David: “The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the one anointed by the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel:
bsb.23:2: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue.
bsb.23:3: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me, ‘He who rules the people with justice, who rules in the fear of God,
bsb.23:4: is like the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn, the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth.’
bsb.23:5: Is not my house right with God? For He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part. Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?
bsb.23:6: But the worthless are all like thorns raked aside, for they can never be gathered by hand.
bsb.23:7: The man who touches them must be armed with iron or with the shaft of a spear. The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie.”
bsb.23:8: These are the names of David’s mighty men: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite was chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed at one time.
bsb.23:9: Next in command was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. As one of the three mighty men, he went with David to taunt the Philistines who had gathered for battle at Pas-dammim. The men of Israel retreated,
bsb.23:10: but Eleazar stood his ground and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and stuck to his sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day. Then the troops returned to him, but only to plunder the dead.
bsb.23:11: And after him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines had banded together near a field full of lentils, Israel’s troops fled from them.
bsb.23:12: But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. So the LORD brought about a great victory.
bsb.23:13: At harvest time, three of the thirty chief men went down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
bsb.23:14: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.
bsb.23:15: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”
bsb.23:16: So the three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out to the LORD,
bsb.23:17: saying, “Far be it from me, O LORD, to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?” So he refused to drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.
bsb.23:18: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab and son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three, and he lifted his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.
bsb.23:19: Was he not more honored than the Three? And he became their commander, even though he was not included among the Three.
bsb.23:20: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
bsb.23:21: He also killed an Egyptian, a huge man. Although the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.
bsb.23:22: These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who won a name alongside the three mighty men.
bsb.23:23: He was most honored among the Thirty, but he did not become one of the Three. And David appointed him over his guard.
bsb.23:24: Now these were members of the Thirty: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
bsb.23:25: Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
bsb.23:26: Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
bsb.23:27: Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
bsb.23:28: Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
bsb.23:29: Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjamites,
bsb.23:30: Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash,
bsb.23:31: Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
bsb.23:32: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen,
bsb.23:33: Jonathan son of Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,
bsb.23:34: Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
bsb.23:35: Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
bsb.23:36: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
bsb.23:37: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,
bsb.23:38: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
bsb.23:39: and Uriah the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.
bsb.24:1: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them, saying, “Go and take a census of Israel and Judah.”
bsb.24:2: So the king said to Joab the commander of his army, who was with him, “Go now throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and register the troops, so that I may know their number.”
bsb.24:3: But Joab replied to the king, “May the LORD your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?”
bsb.24:4: Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army departed from the presence of the king to count the troops of Israel.
bsb.24:5: They crossed the Jordan and camped near Aroer, south of the town in the middle of the valley, and proceeded toward Gad and Jazer.
bsb.24:6: Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and on to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.
bsb.24:7: They went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.
bsb.24:8: At the end of nine months and twenty days, having gone through the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem.
bsb.24:9: And Joab reported to the king the total number of the troops. In Israel there were 800,000 men of valor who drew the sword, and in Judah there were 500,000.
bsb.24:10: After David had numbered the troops, his conscience was stricken and he said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, O LORD, I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
bsb.24:11: When David got up in the morning, a revelation from the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David’s seer:
bsb.24:12: “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’”
bsb.24:13: So Gad went and said to David, “Do you choose to endure three years of famine in your land, three months of fleeing the pursuit of your enemies, or three days of plague upon your land? Now then, think it over and decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”
bsb.24:14: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.”
bsb.24:15: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from that morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.
bsb.24:16: But when the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented from the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
bsb.24:17: When David saw the angel striking down the people, he said to the LORD, “Surely I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? Please, let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house.”
bsb.24:18: And that day Gad came to David and said to him, “Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
bsb.24:19: So David went up at the word of Gad, just as the LORD had commanded.
bsb.24:20: When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him, he went out and bowed facedown before the king.
bsb.24:21: “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” Araunah said. “To buy your threshing floor,” David replied, “that I may build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”
bsb.24:22: Araunah said to David, “My lord the king may take whatever seems good and offer it up. Here are the oxen for a burnt offering and the threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.
bsb.24:23: O king, Araunah gives all these to the king.” He also said to the king, “May the LORD your God accept you.”
bsb.24:24: “No,” replied the king, “I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
bsb.24:25: And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then the LORD answered the prayers on behalf of the land, and the plague upon Israel was halted.

asv.1:1: And it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;
asv.1:2: it came to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul, with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
asv.1:3: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.
asv.1:4: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, The people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
asv.1:5: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?
asv.1:6: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul was leaning upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and the horsemen followed hard after him.
asv.1:7: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I.
asv.1:8: And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
asv.1:9: And he said unto me, Stand, I pray thee, beside me, and slay me; for anguish hath taken hold of me, because my life is yet whole in me.
asv.1:10: So I stood beside him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.
asv.1:11: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:
asv.1:12: and they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Jehovah, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.
asv.1:13: And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite.
asv.1:14: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to put forth thy hand to destroy Jehovah’s anointed?
asv.1:15: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him, so that he died.
asv.1:16: And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain Jehovah’s anointed.
asv.1:17: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son
asv.1:18: (and he bade them teach the children of Judah the song of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jashar):
asv.1:19: Thy glory, O Israel, is slain upon thy high places! How are the mighty fallen!
asv.1:20: Tell it not in Gath, Publish it not in the streets of Ashkelon; Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, Lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
asv.1:21: Ye mountains of Gilboa, Let there be no dew nor rain upon you, neither fields of offerings: For there the shield of the mighty was vilely cast away, The shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.
asv.1:22: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, The bow of Jonathan turned not back, And the sword of Saul returned not empty.
asv.1:23: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, And in their death they were not divided: They were swifter than eagles, They were stronger than lions.
asv.1:24: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, Who clothed you in scarlet delicately, Who put ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
asv.1:25: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan is slain upon thy high places.
asv.1:26: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: Very pleasant hast thou been unto me: Thy love to me was wonderful, Passing the love of women.
asv.1:27: How are the mighty fallen, And the weapons of war perished!
asv.2:1: And it came to pass after this, that David inquired of Jehovah, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And Jehovah said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.
asv.2:2: So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
asv.2:3: And his men that were with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
asv.2:4: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, The men of Jabesh-gilead were they that buried Saul.
asv.2:5: And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabesh-gilead, and said unto them, Blessed be ye of Jehovah, that ye have showed this kindness unto your lord, even unto Saul, and have buried him.
asv.2:6: And now Jehovah show lovingkindness and truth unto you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.
asv.2:7: Now therefore let your hands be strong, and be ye valiant; for Saul your lord is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.
asv.2:8: Now Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, had taken Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
asv.2:9: and he made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
asv.2:10: Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.
asv.2:11: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
asv.2:12: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
asv.2:13: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met them by the pool of Gibeon; and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
asv.2:14: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men, I pray thee, arise and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.
asv.2:15: Then they arose and went over by number: twelve for Benjamin, and for Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
asv.2:16: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon.
asv.2:17: And the battle was very sore that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
asv.2:18: And the three sons of Zeruiah were there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.
asv.2:19: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner.
asv.2:20: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Is it thou, Asahel? And he answered, It is I.
asv.2:21: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armor. But Asahel would not turn aside from following him.
asv.2:22: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?
asv.2:23: Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him in the body, so that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.
asv.2:24: But Joab and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that lieth before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
asv.2:25: And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one band, and stood on the top of a hill.
asv.2:26: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from following their brethren?
asv.2:27: And Joab said, As God liveth, if thou hadst not spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone away, nor followed every one his brother.
asv.2:28: So Joab blew the trumpet; and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.
asv.2:29: And Abner and his men went all that night through the Arabah; and they passed over the Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
asv.2:30: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel.
asv.2:31: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner’s men, so that three hundred and threescore men died.
asv.2:32: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, which was in Beth-lehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and the day brake upon them at Hebron.
asv.3:1: Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: and David waxed stronger and stronger, but the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker.
asv.3:2: And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his first-born was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
asv.3:3: and his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
asv.3:4: and the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
asv.3:5: and the sixth, Ithream, of Eglah, David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
asv.3:6: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong in the house of Saul.
asv.3:7: Now Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and Ish-bosheth said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father’s concubine?
asv.3:8: Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ish-bosheth, and said, Am I a dog’s head that belongeth to Judah? This day do I show kindness unto the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David; and yet thou chargest me this day with a fault concerning this woman.
asv.3:9: God do so to Abner, and more also, if, as Jehovah hath sworn to David, I do not even so to him;
asv.3:10: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beer-sheba.
asv.3:11: And he could not answer Abner another word, because he feared him.
asv.3:12: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose is the land? saying also, Make thy league with me, and, behold, my hand shall be with thee, to bring about all Israel unto thee.
asv.3:13: And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee; but one thing I require of thee: that is, thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal, Saul’s daughter, when thou comest to see my face.
asv.3:14: And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, saying, Deliver me my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to me for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
asv.3:15: And Ish-bosheth sent, and took her from her husband, even from Paltiel the son of Laish.
asv.3:16: And her husband went with her, weeping as he went, and followed her to Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return: and he returned.
asv.3:17: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, In times past ye sought for David to be king over you:
asv.3:18: now then do it; for Jehovah hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.
asv.3:19: And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and to the whole house of Benjamin.
asv.3:20: So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that were with him a feast.
asv.3:21: And Abner said unto David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel unto my lord the king, that they may make a covenant with thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thy soul desireth. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.
asv.3:22: And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from a foray, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner was not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone in peace.
asv.3:23: When Joab and all the host that was with him were come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him away, and he is gone in peace.
asv.3:24: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came unto thee; why is it that thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?
asv.3:25: Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou doest.
asv.3:26: And when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah: but David knew it not.
asv.3:27: And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the midst of the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there in the body, so that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
asv.3:28: And afterward, when David heard it, he said, I and my kingdom are guiltless before Jehovah for ever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner:
asv.3:29: let it fall upon the head of Joab, and upon all his father’s house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth by the sword, or that lacketh bread.
asv.3:30: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.
asv.3:31: And David said to Joab, and to all the people that were with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David followed the bier.
asv.3:32: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.
asv.3:33: And the king lamented for Abner, and said, Should Abner die as a fool dieth?
asv.3:34: Thy hands were not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: As a man falleth before the children of iniquity, so didst thou fall. And all the people wept again over him.
asv.3:35: And all the people came to cause David to eat bread while it was yet day; but David sware, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or aught else, till the sun be down.
asv.3:36: And all the people took notice of it, and it pleased them; as whatsoever the king did pleased all the people.
asv.3:37: So all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.
asv.3:38: And the king said unto his servants, Know ye not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?
asv.3:39: And I am this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me: Jehovah reward the evil-doer according to his wickedness.
asv.4:1: And when Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands became feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.
asv.4:2: And Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin (for Beeroth also is reckoned to Benjamin:
asv.4:3: and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and have been sojourners there until this day).
asv.4:4: Now Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son that was lame of his feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel; and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.
asv.4:5: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, as he took his rest at noon.
asv.4:6: And they came thither into the midst of the house, as though they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him in the body: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
asv.4:7: Now when they came into the house, as he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and went by the way of the Arabah all night.
asv.4:8: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold, the head of Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul, thine enemy, who sought thy life; and Jehovah hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.
asv.4:9: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As Jehovah liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
asv.4:10: when one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, which was the reward I gave him for his tidings.
asv.4:11: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed, shall I not now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?
asv.4:12: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth, and buried it in the grave of Abner in Hebron.
asv.5:1: Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.
asv.5:2: In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was thou that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and Jehovah said to thee, Thou shalt be shepherd of my people Israel, and thou shalt be prince over Israel.
asv.5:3: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a covenant with them in Hebron before Jehovah: and they anointed David king over Israel.
asv.5:4: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
asv.5:5: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months; and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.
asv.5:6: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither; thinking, David cannot come in hither.
asv.5:7: Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion; the same is the city of David.
asv.5:8: And David said on that day, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites, let him get up to the watercourse, and smite the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul. Wherefore they say, There are the blind and the lame; he cannot come into the house.
asv.5:9: And David dwelt in the stronghold, and called it the city of David. And David built round about from Millo and inward.
asv.5:10: And David waxed greater and greater; for Jehovah, the God of hosts, was with him.
asv.5:11: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar-trees, and carpenters, and masons; and they built David a house.
asv.5:12: And David perceived that Jehovah had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel’s sake.
